• Support post-closing activities, including revisions to CDs or ALTA statements and overall file completion.

• Manage an active pipeline of files, prioritizing tasks to meet deadlines and established service level agreements.

Job Overview
We are looking for an Accounts Receivable & Collections Specialist to support an Australian client with growing transaction volumes. In this role, you will manage overdue customer accounts through direct phone and email contact, secure payment commitments, and help reduce outstanding debt. You will work closely with the client's finance team on shared customer accounts and own the month-end credit insurance reporting on overdue accounts.
Key Responsibilities

•
Overdue Account Follow-Up: Confidently contact customers with overdue accounts by phone and email to understand reasons for non-payment and secure payment commitments that reduce outstanding debt.

•
Team Collaboration: Work closely with the client's finance team, who handle routine collections before the due date, to ensure a smooth handover of accounts once they become overdue and consistent communication with customers.

Internal Dispute Resolution: Coordinate with internal managers so that invoice disputes and contract requirements are addressed in a timely manner.

Clear Account Communication: Clearly and accurately explain payment terms, outstanding balances, and dispute resolutions across phone and email.

Ledger Reconciliation: Reconcile customer ledgers, including offsetting credit notes against invoices and allocating unapplied payments.

•
Credit Limit Monitoring: Monitor customer balances to ensure agreed credit limits are not breached; run risk assessments, review credit files, and flag high-risk accounts.

•
Doubtful Debt Provision: Calculate doubtful debt provision requirements based on company policy.

Functional Skill: Strong collections and negotiation skills, with the ability to handle difficult conversations and customer pushback while keeping relationships professional; commercially aware of the cash flow and bad-debt impact of overdue accounts.

Soft Skills: Assertive yet diplomatic, an active listener who can identify the root cause of payment delays and negotiate realistic payment solutions on the spot. Proactive, organized, and collaborative.

Language: Excellent spoken English with clear pronunciation, professional phrasing, and the ability to build rapport easily over the phone; strong written English for email correspondence.

•
Education: Bachelor's degree in Accountancy, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field is preferred.

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

- Triage support cases including directing users to previous answers, code examples, documentation, or escalating to specific technical or business team members.

- Monitor multiple feedback channels, e.g. Github Issues & Discussions (check them here: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues).

- Identify where internal tooling might be developed or obtained to improve support efficiency.

You are:

- Experienced in customer support, with 3+ years of experience providing developer support to technical customers.

- Proficient in SQL (ideally PostgreSQL). You feel comfortable with complex SQL queries. If you have a database administration experience, it’s a plus.

- Excellent communication skills and fluency in English.

- Skilled in using Linux/Unix operating systems and the command line.

- Experienced working with GitHub Issues and Discussions.

- Bonus points if you're familiar with popular JavaScript frameworks like React, Vue, and Svelte and have some experience with Node.js.

- Having a degree in Computer Science is a plus too.

TIMEZONES & LOGISTICS

- It’s a full-time position permanently, with four 10-hour shifts covering weekends during APAC Hours: 00:00-10:00 UTC

- We are primarily looking for someone in Southeast Asia or India time zones for this shift.

- This position covers Friday → Monday based on the above UTC times, so this may vary slightly for your specific timezone.

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

- Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

- Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

- Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

- Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning-courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

- ~400 team members

- 60+ countries

- 20+ languages spoken

- Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

- 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support-not replace-existing tools and communities.

Company description
 
Service Measure (SM) is a field data collection company founded in 2013 in New York. 
 
We collect data where automation is not possible. We count features, take pictures, make videos, record speech, and scan areas for every detail you need to make more informed decisions. Our field data collection teams are spread across Europe and North America, ready to accept new challenges.
 
Project objective
 
The goal of the project is to help collect images of streets, main points of interest and public areas in the USA. The project is performed on cars with 360 cameras mounted on top that image the area around the vehicle and store those images on computers inside the vehicle. Later, this data will be used to enhance one the most popular online maps in the world.
 
The data collectors will be given specific routes around public streets and areas, specifically targeting commercial districts and historical sites. Due to poor weather conditions some areas will be visited multiple times in order to collect the best quality of imaging. The project is expected to last from 3 to 6 months and will cover different data collection areas. 
 
The ideal candidate enjoys driving, knows well the area, traffic trends, is highly responsible and reliable.
 
The schedule expected on the project is Monday-Friday, 8 hours/day 40 hours per week. Due to weather downtime, work on weekends is possible.

title: Menlo Fellows
description:
The Role
Menlo builds open source and production AI systems, from the brain, to developer facing tools to the runtime infrastructure and humanoid platform underneath. This fellowship is deliberately open ended: tell us your strengths and we'll match you to high impact work across software engineering, systems, applied AI, or research. You'll be hands on from day one, with a Menlo engineer or researcher directly responsible for your mentorship and your results. You own deliverables at the same level as the team you join. We expect you to contribute, not observe.
This is a paid internship program that runs year round. Candidates go through a rigorous interview process and get matched with a senior researcher or engineer working on real world problems.
What You'll Do

• Own a real project end to end, from problem definition through implementation, testing, and documentation.

• Ship production grade work in one or more areas: product engineering, systems, infrastructure, applied AI, or research.

• Work on core Menlo projects, including developer tooling, model runtime and performance, automation, and reliability improvements.

• Debug real issues across codebases and environments, and propose fixes that improve correctness, performance, and maintainability.

• Write clear docs, runbooks, or internal notes that make your work easy for the team to adopt.

• Collaborate closely with engineers and researchers through code reviews and technical discussions.

What We Look For

• University, high school or mid-career individuals looking for a crash course in physical AI and robotics

• The ability to read unfamiliar codebases and make safe, well scoped changes.

• Practical debugging skills: you can isolate problems and validate fixes.

• A grasp of software or hardware engineering basics: testing, version control, and review.

• A high ownership mindset and the ability to work independently with fast feedback loops.

• Above all, we hire for slope: how fast you grow matters more than where you start.

Logistics

• 3 months minimum, based in one of our offices: San Francisco, Ho Chi Minh City, or Singapore

• Paid role.

• Open to pre university and university students.

• You'll need existing work authorization for your office location, as we don't provide visa sponsorship for this role.

Why Join Menlo
You'll do real work that ships, not busywork on the bench. Genuine ownership, direct mentorship from the people building Asimov, and a chance to prove yourself on hard problems alongside some of the most curious and driven people you'll meet. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.
A Note on AI
You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.
Equal Opportunity and Accommodations
We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

description:
Footprint is the agentic platform that learns your compliance program and runs it end to end.

Compliance teams at banks and fintechs are drowning in financial crimes investigations. Transaction volumes are surging, regulators keep raising the bar, and the work still runs on manual review queues stitched together from legacy vendors. Percy, our agentic system, learns each team's procedures and makes the same calls their analysts would: clearing false positives, escalating real risk, writing the case narrative, and documenting every decision for audit. It cuts review workloads by 70%+.

The harder problem is underneath. Every investigation is grounded in the data sources compliance teams already trust, and every case commits to an organizational memory that compounds - so a pattern one analyst caught in March surfaces automatically in October, across KYC, EDD, sanctions, and monitoring. Whether the team is five analysts or 500, they share one brain. Every memory carries provenance. Agents propose; humans approve. That's four years of identity infrastructure sitting under the agent, and it's the part nobody can bolt on later.

We're backed by QED, Index, and Box Group, and trusted by FDIC- and OCC-regulated banks plus fintechs like Bilt, Nuvei, and MoonPay. We 5x'd revenue last year. The team is small, senior, and ships fast.

The short version: you'll own a book of Footprint customers from the day they sign: working alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers as they get each customer live, meeting with each team regularly and growing what they do with Footprint. This is our first Account Manager, on-site in New York, reporting to Peter Sweeney. Base $145K-$155K, OTE $190K-$205K, plus equity.

 

The Role

We're hiring our first Account Manager to look after Footprint's customers once they sign.

Most customers start with Percy on one workflow and add more over time. When a team you work with wants to add a workflow or a product, you scope it with a Forward Deployed Engineer and close the deal. When a different team or business line at the same customer gets interested, you bring in an Account Executive and work it together.

You'll report directly to Peter Sweeney, our Head of GTM Strategy and Post Sales.

 

What You'll Own

Your book of accounts. You own each customer relationship from signature through every renewal. When an Account Executive brings on a new team at one of your customers, that team joins your book once it signs

From signature to go-live. The Account Executive introduces you once a contract is signed. While a Forward Deployed Engineer gets the customer live, you're their main contact, and once they're live the account is yours

Getting customers what they need. When something comes up, you get the right person at Footprint on it and stay with it until the customer has their answer

Regular check-ins. You meet with each team on a steady rhythm, bring them what's new in the product and hear what's changing on their side. Those conversations are where the next opportunities show up

Growth inside your accounts. Selling new products and new use cases to the teams you manage is yours, and so is making what they already run work harder for them. The opportunity is often a workflow the customer hasn't brought to Footprint yet. You find it, scope it with a Forward Deployed Engineer and close it

The function itself. How we run onboarding, check-ins and the handoff from Account Executives is yours to set

 

Must-Have

- You've worked alongside engineers on customer implementations and kept working with them afterward to get customer questions to the right person

- You've kept a regular cadence of check-ins across your accounts, and customers used those meetings to bring you what they wanted next

The role will own key corporate FP&A deliverables, including consolidated forecasting, cash flow modeling and forecasting, Board and ELT reporting, PE sponsor and portfolio company reporting, and GAAP-to-non-GAAP bridges.
Our approach to FP&A is simple: understand what happened, determine why it matters, and help the business decide what to do next.
In this role, that means taking inputs from across the FP&A organization and translating them into an accurate, coherent company-level view of performance and outlook. This person will work closely across FP&A, Accounting, Treasury, and the broader Office of the CFO, with significant exposure to senior leadership.

About the role:
Amber is looking for a UX Designer to help bring a high-quality AA Unreal Engine 5 game to a cloud streaming platform. It's a large narrative game, built on one of the most recognized entertainment franchises.
The story and content are locked. Your job is to adapt UX/UI and controls. The goal is a game that's easy to pick up and keeps its pacing. The core direction is only prototyped, and many open problems remain. You'll work alongside UX designers, engineers, tech artists, QAs, and producers. This is a hands-on role: mapping, wireframes, and specs, delivered at volume and largely on your own.
This is a remote contract engagement, expected to run about 2 months, with a possible extension. You'll need to be productive within your first week. Preferred working hours are 7am-4pm Mexico City time. European candidates should overlap with a minimum of 7am-12pm Mexico City time.
What to expect from the process:

• Profile Preselection: Our Talent Acquisition team will review your profile.

• Talent Acquisition Screening: Selected candidates will be contacted to undergo an initial interview to discuss their experience, skills, and fit for the role.

• Test: Qualified candidates will be invited to complete an assessment to demonstrate their abilities.

• Interviews: Finalists will participate in technical and cultural interviews to assess their proficiency and compatibility with our team.

The quest (what you will do):

• Map every interaction in the game to a touch controller.

• Design controller layouts, prompts, and accessibility options in Figma.

• Build onboarding that teaches the controls to players new to games.

• Define system flows, such as settings, pause, and disconnect.

• Write implementation specs for engineering. Run consistency passes across the full game.

• Turn playtest findings into design changes.

• Flag usability risks early. Present options backed by evidence.

The skills (required qualifications):

• At least 5 years as a UX designer in games, with at least one shipped game.

• A portfolio that shows game UX work, such as player flows, wireframes, and interaction specs.

• Proven experience designing touch controls for games.

• Experience designing game UX, preferably for console or TV.

• Onboarding design for casual players.

• Strong Figma skills, including wireframes.

• Working knowledge of game accessibility practices, especially input simplification and alternative controls.

• Comfortable making decisions with incomplete information.

• Clear communication in English, spoken and written.

Nice to have:

• Second-screen or phone-as-controller UX.

• Cloud gaming projects, or input design that holds up under latency.

• Work on narrative or cinematic games.

• Designing to platform requirements, such as console certification rules.

• Motion controls or haptics design.

The Reward:

• A fun and dynamic industry where you can make a difference.

• Professional and friendly work environment.

• Awesome and talented colleagues.

• Support from all your teammates.

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

What is the Engineering Academy?

The Engineering Academy is designed to accelerate your tech career at Vinted. This intensive, hands-on programme features training sessions led by our very own experts, who will mentor and guide you through our technology and ways of working.

The programme kicks off with a 2-month induction , covering a broad range of topics - from best practices with Git to understanding how Kubernetes operates at Vinted. It’s a challenging yet rewarding experience that will give you a solid foundation to succeed in your future teams!

The Engineering Academy runs for 6 months and includes:

• 2 months of technical induction: collaborate with other Academy students in product teams, refine your skills & knowledge with a mentor & in technical workshops.

• 4 months in a real Vinted engineering team: experience day-to-day life of a Vinted engineer.

• Ongoing learning sessions: join learning sessions and build your personal skills.

You’ll be hired on a 6 months contract , with the opportunity to join Vinted permanently after completing the Academy and continue growing your career with the skills you’ve gained.

Want to learn more? Check out engineering.vinted.com to see what we’re up to.

Who are we looking for?

The Vinted Engineering Academy is where we grow our tech talent in  Android Engineering. Whether you’re a student, recent graduate, self-taught coder, or something else, this is the place for you.

We’re looking for people with some coding skills and a passion for all things engineering - those who are just starting their careers in this area and are eager to learn, grow, and make an impact.

When?

Our  Spring   Engineering Academy begins on March 1, 2027 . You will be expected to be available full time (0.8 contract option for University students is possible).

In this position, you'll

• Work on features for our main Vinted app using Kotlin.

• Use comprehensive testing methodologies, including unit tests, integration tests, snapshot tests, and UI tests.

• Learn to work on a large-scale mobile application with millions of users.

• Have a chance to work closely with an experienced engineer who will help you grow.

• Collaborate with other software engineers through GitHub pull requests and code reviews.

• Improve our user experience by implementing product changes, often via experimentation.

• Apply Agile and Scrum principles in your work.

About you

• Some experience building Android apps. Heard about Kotlin? Awesome!

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets - the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

THE ROLE

9fin's buy-side clients are the capital behind the credit markets. Credit funds, CLO managers, private credit platforms, and distressed investors run research, underwriting, portfolio monitoring, and relative value workflows that are deep and specialised. They are actively excited about what AI can unlock. Our job is to make that potential real inside their investment teams.

The Forward Deployed Investor is the person who does it. You are a domain expert who has done the work yourself, and you can credibly sit across the table from a portfolio manager, a private credit underwriter, or a distressed analyst and say: "Here is how this changes the way you invest."

You will work with 9fin's most strategic buy-side clients, drive deep adoption of our existing AI capabilities across the investment process, and become a critical voice in shaping what we build next. Every client engagement is a source of product intelligence. The insights you bring back from the front line will directly influence 9fin's AI product roadmap and sharpen how we win the next generation of buy-side accounts.

- Build 9fin's AI into those workflows. Take the identified insertion points and build them out using 9fin's toolkit: in-platform capabilities, MCP integrations, agents, and future capabilities as they ship. Weighted by workflow depth, not count. Iterate based on real usage behaviour, not intended usage.

- Drive adoption at your served accounts. Onboard named users across investment, research, and risk. Run enablement sessions with power users, identify and support champions inside the client. Monitor active usage and address dormant seats before they become churn signals. Review adoption monthly with client champions and quarterly with the CIO, head of research, or equivalent sponsor.

- Feed the field back into 9fin. Every deployment produces structured intelligence, fed to two consumers. First, product and engineering: prioritised requests tied to specific account and workflow context, patterns extracted across deployments. Second, the wider GTM cycle: case studies, demo assets, workflow evidence, and competitive intelligence that sharpen the next GTM cycle.

- Spot expansion. Identify opportunities inside served accounts for new users, new use cases, new departments, or new products. Document with context and hand to Account Management for commercial follow-up.

Field Systems Engineer - Military Health IT (DDIL)
Location: Remote - United States (Home Station)
Travel: Frequent travel, including overseas and austere locations
Security Clearance: Active Secret required
Keep Critical Systems Running. Support Military Medicine in the Field.
Military medical teams depend on technology that works, even when network connectivity is limited or unavailable.
Rackner is seeking a Field Systems Engineer to support Joint Operational Medicine Information Systems (JOMIS) and related technology in disconnected, degraded, intermittent, or limited-connectivity (DDIL) environments. You'll help prepare, maintain, secure, and restore equipment used during exercises, system fielding, and deployed operations.
This is an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys hands-on problem-solving, takes ownership of challenging technical work, and wants to contribute to military healthcare beyond traditional office environments.
What You'll Do

• Prepare, configure, troubleshoot, and restore medical IT equipment supporting fielding activities, exercises, and deployed operations.

• Administer Windows and Linux environments, including system maintenance, patching, audit-log analysis, and technical troubleshooting.

• Diagnose networking, infrastructure, and hardware issues in locations where connectivity and technical resources may be limited.

• Prepare and validate offline system packages, supporting operational continuity and data reconciliation when connectivity is restored.

• Support system security, including DISA STIG readiness, vulnerability assessment activities, and implementation of approved hardening requirements.

• Conduct site surveys and installation planning, provide primary or backup engineering coverage for assigned deployments, and support authorized urgent field assignments.

Required Qualifications

• Four or more years of field systems engineering experience involving Windows, Linux, networking, and deployable hardware.

• Hands-on experience with systems administration, troubleshooting, and restoration in field or operational environments.

• Experience with DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and the Assured Compliance Assessment Solution (ACAS).

• Current qualification meeting the applicable DoD 8140 / IAT Level II requirement, such as CompTIA Security+ CE or an accepted equivalent.

• Active U.S. Government Secret security clearance.

• Willingness and ability to travel frequently, including internationally and to austere locations, as required.

Preferred Qualifications

• Supporting JOMIS or military medical IT during fielding activities or deployed operations.

• Experience with tactical networking or deployable communications infrastructure.

• DDIL testing, chaos testing, or related system resilience activities.

At Rackner , you'll have the opportunity to apply your technical expertise to work that supports critical federal missions.
You'll collaborate with engineers and operational professionals, take ownership of meaningful field engineering challenges, and help maintain dependable technology in environments where reliability matters.
We value practical problem-solving, technical accountability, teamwork, and continuous professional development.

• Company-supported certifications and professional development opportunities.

• 401(k) with a 100% company match on eligible contributions up to 6%.

• Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance.

• Paid time off and paid holidays.

• Home-office equipment and remote-work support.

• Fitness and wellness reimbursement.

• Weekly pay and company team events.

Benefits are subject to eligibility, applicable policies, and plan terms.
Work Arrangement
This position is remote from a U.S.-based home station but requires frequent travel to support fielding activities, exercises, and deployed operations.

About Us

Red Cell Partners is an incubation firm building and investing in rapidly scalable technology-led companies that are bringing revolutionary advancements to market in three distinct practice areas: healthcare, cyber, and national security. United by a shared sense of duty and deep belief in the power of innovation, Red Cell is developing powerful tools and solutions to address our Nation’s most pressing problems.

ABOUT DEFCON AI
RESILIENCE IN THE FACE OF DISRUPTION. DEFCON AI is an insights company that leverages artificial intelligence, mathematical optimization, data analytics, and software engineering for resilient optimization of complex systems.
In today’s dynamically changing world, DEFCON AI’s technology aligns outcomes with operational goals, better decision making, and empowers customers to anticipate assess, and mitigate the impacts of disruptions.

About the Role

As QA Engineer you will own quality for an AI-enabled decision-support system: the test plan, the automated coverage, and the evidence that what was delivered is what was specified. Product defines the acceptance criteria. You build the executable version of it , and you hold engineering, platform, and everyone else delivering the work accountable to it.

This role sits on the product side of the organization, not the engineering side. You will report through the Product Lead and take direction from product, while working with engineering and platform every day. A tester embedded in engineering tends to verify what was built, because the implementation is what they see. This role verifies what was specified. A test suite written from the code will pass while still missing what the customer asked for.

That reporting line does not lower the engineering bar. You will write code and build real automation rather than managing test cases, and you will need enough fluency in the application code to test it well. As the first dedicated quality engineering hire you are establishing the approach rather than inheriting one, so we want someone with a clear point of view on how testing should work. We build with current tooling and expect the same, including AI assistance in our own engineering practice.

This is a fully remote role with occasional travel (up to 25%) to DEFCON AI HQ, customer sites, and vendor facilities as required.

Key Responsibilities

Test Strategy and Acceptance Criteria

• Own the system test plan covering functional, integration, performance, and load testing, and maintain it as a formal deliverable

• Translate the acceptance criteria set by product into executable tests

• Review acceptance criteria with product before development begins, and identify requirements that are ambiguous or not verifiable as written

• Hold engineering, platform, and partner teams accountable to the acceptance criteria, and define what evidence must exist before a change is considered complete

• Work alongside the engineering team day to day, close enough to test their work well and independent enough to report what the testing shows

• Plan and coordinate user acceptance testing with the customer, and track findings through to resolution

Test Automation and Coverage

• Build and maintain automated test suites, and integrate them into the CI/CD pipeline as release gates

• Establish and hold an automated coverage standard, and report against it

• Build performance and load testing that validates the system under its expected user load

• Maintain regression coverage across releases

Measurement and Evidence

• Build and maintain labeled evaluation sets, working with subject-matter experts whose time is limited

• Design and run sampled audits confirming that automated decisions were correct

• Measure and report what the system misses alongside what it gets right

• Measure how often users override the system, and report the trend

• Document how each committed measure is computed, on what data, and what evidence accompanies a release

title: Salesforce Solutions Consultant
description:
Salesforce Solutions Consultant

Solutions | United States (Remote) | Full-Time | NAM

Who We Are
Bluprintx (BPX) is a global, AI-powered consultancy built to design and deliver the intelligent front office for CMO and CRO executives. We are private equity-backed and scaling fast, with 300 active customers across 10 countries and more than 1,750 implementations. We connect people, technology, and AI to turn fragmentation into performance, partnering with global leaders to modernize how marketing, CRM, content, AI & Data connect. At BPX, we hire operators and specialists who thrive at the intersection of commercial strategy and technical execution.
What We Do
We help the world's most ambitious companies, including Uber Eats, BNY, and Xerox, untangle the operational complexity that slows enterprise growth. As a Gold Adobe Solution Partner and Salesforce Summit Partner, we deliver strategy and implementation across the full front office. Our proprietary methodology builds sustainable enabled ecosystems that maximize ROI and accelerate speed to market. By embedding AI into commercial workflows, we help clients move faster and stay ahead.
The Role
You'll be the person prospects watch when they want to see Salesforce solve their problem in a live org. In this presales seat you design, build and deliver tailored demonstrations across the Salesforce Core platform, turning what you learn in discovery into a working story inside a live org. A typical week mixes discovery calls, demo builds, RFP responses and deal strategy sessions with our Account Executives. You'll field the hard product, architecture and integration questions in the room, then work with our delivery team so what gets sold is scoped to land. It's a hands-on role for someone who would rather configure the product than talk about it, with occasional travel for customer meetings, demos and team events.
What you'll do

• Build tailored demos end to end, mapped to each prospect's own requirements and use cases.

• Own the demo orgs, keeping environments, sample data and reusable scenarios current and presentation-ready.

• Lead discovery sessions that surface business pain, technical requirements and success criteria, then shape the solution story.

• Partner with Account Executives on solution strategy, value positioning and technical objections through the sales cycle.

• Answer RFPs and RFIs and technical questionnaires, and support proof-of-concept and pilot engagements.

• Keep proposals realistic with delivery and product teams, so every solution is scoped accurately and set up to implement well.

• Bring new releases into your demos as the Salesforce roadmap moves, especially Agentforce and Data Cloud.

What you'll bring

• Hands-on Salesforce depth: 5 to 7 years configuring, building and demonstrating on the platform.

• Presales experience as a Sales Engineer, Solutions Consultant or Presales Consultant, or in a demo-focused role.

• Multi-cloud range to demo Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Data Cloud (Data 360), Experience Cloud and Agentforce with confidence.

• Consultative discovery skills that connect a business problem to the right platform capability.

• Presence in the room to tell a clear story, run a live demo and handle technical questions on the spot.

• Self-directed remote working, comfortable running your own week across a fully distributed team.

• Bonus points for Salesforce certifications (Administrator, Sales, Service or Data Cloud Consultant, Agentforce Specialist) or partner and SI experience.

Why this role, why now

Salesforce clients want to see Agentforce and Data Cloud working against their own use cases before they commit. As a Salesforce Summit Partner growing on private equity backing, BPX gives you the platform breadth and the customer conversations to show them, across Sales, Service, Data and Experience Cloud.

Additional information
Benefits include medical insurance, 401(k), PTO, sick leave and remote working.

title: Member of Technical Staff, ML Platform (Evals)
description:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems - robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an ML infrastructure engineer to own model evaluation at Runway, end to end. Every decision we make about a model - which checkpoint to keep training, what to ship to millions of users, which datamix and architecture shows the most promise - rests on evals. Today that work is spread across the organization. You'll turn it into one platform.

Your job will be to design and build the systems that generate samples at scale, score them with automated metrics and human annotations, track results across checkpoints and releases, and put the answers in front of researchers in minutes rather than days. You'll define what "better" means operationally - how we measure it, how confident we are, and how a result becomes a ship/no-ship decision.

You'll be embedded within research teams as a member of ML Platform, and you'll set the technical direction for evals across the company. This is an extremely high-leverage role: the quality of our models is bounded by how well we can measure them.

A PEEK AT OUR TECHNICAL STACK

Our inference and training code is written in Python (PyTorch) and is cloud-native. We leverage multiple clouds and use a combination of Kubernetes native and home-grown tooling for efficient job orchestration.

We’re big users of agentic development and operations. We have a robust internal platform and provide broad access to the latest models and harnesses.

You’ll have access to best-in-class models, agents, GPUs, storage and cloud services you need to drive a world class evaluation pipeline that helps us deliver frontier models.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the evaluation platform end to end: the tooling and systems required to generate, annotate, review and adapt at frontier scale

- Define the CLIs, APIs, GUIs and storage layers required to make this process seamless, fast, sophisticated and collaborative

- Work directly with research teams on video, image, audio, agents, and robotics to understand what they need to measure and build it, then generalize the result into the platform

- Help set the standards for how we evaluate models at Runway: reproducibility, metric definitions, reporting formats, and when a result is trustworthy enough to act on

- Support broad adoption of the platform and its integration throughout Runway’s research efforts across training, production model serving and more

- Contribute broadly as a member of the ML Platform team to tools and systems that help Runway train and serve frontier models

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- 5+ years of experience building ML infrastructure or data platforms in production environments, with at least some of that time spent on evaluation, experimentation, or benchmarking systems

- Strong Python and PyTorch, and hands-on experience running

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale.

You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees.

We’re looking for someone with:

- Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail.

- Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows.

- Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance.

- Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures.

- Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination.

- Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results.

- Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations.

In this role, you will:

- Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements.

- Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue.

- Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues.

- Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions.

- Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners.

title: Senior KYB Specialist - Business Account
description:
About us

Traditional banking has never really given you control over your financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance. That means making financial services easy and accessible for over 6.5M users. We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close. We follow the same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world. If you own outcomes rather than tasks, stay close to what users need, and refuse to wait for someone else to fix what's broken - you'll find people here who work exactly in the same way. And together, you'll build something worth being proud of.

What you'll be doing

As our Senior KYB Specialist - Business Account in Barcelona, you'll bring strong specialist expertise in corporate KYB and business accounts to shape our risk-based onboarding and ongoing due diligence processes. Reporting to the KYB Manager, you will serve as a senior point of reference for Business Account KYB-applying sound judgment to complex cases and connecting KYB needs directly with the teams building the product.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

- Contribute to the KYB framework - Shape risk-based onboarding and ongoing due diligence processes for business customers, accounting for the specific characteristics and risks of the products they use.

- Support customer and entity assessments - Apply specialist judgment to complex ownership structures, legal representatives, and authorised persons to help the team evaluate relationships, authority, and relevant risks.

- Contribute to lifecycle reviews - Define how customer information and risk assessments are reviewed and updated over time, including when existing customers adopt additional products.

- Support complex KYB decisions - Provide specialist judgment on unusual, higher-risk, or unclear cases, guiding decisions and escalations within our agreed framework.

- Turn regulation and risk requirements into clear ways of working - Partner with relevant teams to translate regulatory expectations and risk appetite into practical checks, evidence requirements, decision criteria, review rules, and escalation points.

- Develop procedures and team capability - Create practical procedures, playbooks, and guidance that enable the team to work consistently and independently, while sharing case learnings, delivering training, and offering specialist support to colleagues.

- Work with Product and control teams - Translate KYB requirements into workflows, tools, and procedures, contributing to testing and operational readiness while identifying opportunities for standardisation, automation, or necessary manual review.

- Support ongoing improvement - Analyse case trends, operational data, and Quality team findings to spot recurring issues and improve controls, procedures, guidance, and customer journeys.

- Work across the organisation - Collaborate with Product, Compliance, FinCrime, Legal, Risk, and Operations to build solutions that balance risk, customer experience, and operational scalability.

Who we're looking for

This role needs someone who brings deep corporate KYB ownership, thrives on solving complex regulatory puzzles, and knows how to turn specialist judgment into scalable, practical workflows.

- Experience - At least 5 years in corporate KYB, business banking, fintech, payments, or another regulated financial-services environment.

- Entity & ownership assessment - Hands-on experience evaluating legal entities and complex ownership structures, including UBOs, legal representatives, authorised persons, and non-standard corporate arrangements.

- Product-specific due diligence - Proven background in KYB or customer due diligence for business accounts, payment accounts, or similar regulated financial products, understanding how product features impact customer risk.

title: Program Manager, Housing Counseling
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.

JOB OVERVIEW
The Program Manager, Housing Counseling provides technical and administrative support for the development of network-wide Housing Counseling toolkits, curricula, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that build IRC’s capacity to deliver and sustain housing counseling services under IRC’s Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Housing Counseling Multi-State Organization (MSO). The role will support local offices in expanding housing counseling activities that strengthen client housing stabilization and homelessness prevention. This role will also support IRC’s housing programs and services in collaboration with the HQ Resettlement Team, Economic Empowerment Team, and other teams across RAI US. The position sits within the HQ Resettlement Housing Team and reports to the Director, Initial Resettlement.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

• Draft and update Housing Counseling curricula, toolkits, and SOPs aligned with HUD regulations and guidance (e.g., Handbook 7610.1 and 24 CFR part 214) and IRC’s Strategy 100, for use by housing counseling staff across IRC’s U.S. network and those preparing to take the HUD Housing Counselor Certification exam.

• Prepare client-facing housing counseling curriculum materials for in-person counseling and workshop, plus online LMS platforms.

• Maintain and update Resource Navigation tools that map available local, state, and federal housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, and rental assistance resources across the network.

• Help plan and facilitate Housing Counseling and counselor certification training, as well as other IRC housing training, peer learning, and knowledge-sharing opportunities across the network, including through the Monthly Housing Call, Communities of Practice, Switchboard, and similar forums.

• Serve as a first point of contact for day-to-day operational questions, providing technical assistance to support offices in launching, expanding, and sustaining housing counseling programming and other IRC housing programs and their requirements.

• Respond to office requests for guidance on housing counseling program design, documentation, and compliance, applying established HUD requirements and IRC guidance, and escalating complex or ambiguous cases as needed.

• Collaborate with the HQ Housing Team, HQ Economic Empowerment Team, Resettlement colleagues, and other HQ departments (e.g., Preferred Communities and Policy) to support the alignment of housing counseling programming with IRC’s broader housing and resettlement strategy.

• Support data collection, outcome tracking, and HUD-required reporting (e.g., HUD Form 9902), compile and summarize program data to flag trends and gaps for program improvements, and contribute to housing related grant proposals, donor reports and applications, including mapping local funding opportunities in collaboration with field offices and HQ staff.

• Draft standardized practices and quality assurance protocols (e.g., case file review guidance, supervisory monitoring templates) that align affiliate housing counseling practice with HUD Housing
